decisions.reason: The spectral-theorem supplier defines M=(ker T)^perp and also supplies M^perp as a subset of ker T. Symmetry of orthogonality gives the reverse inclusion ker T as a subset of M^perp, so M^perp=ker T. Thus the equality used in steps 3.1 and 4.1 is a valid consequence of the cited interface.

The local natural-number convention includes zero, so the former phrase 'for each n' made the radius 1/n undefined at n=0. The construction only needs finite nets at positive reciprocal scales; restricting both occurrences to integers n>=1 yields the same countable dense union and repairs the proof without changing the theorem's claim.

The displayed multiplication specialization asserted a Frechet derivative for a merely normed algebra, but the library's derivative interface and the proved general theorem require Banach domains and codomains. Completeness is not automatic for a bounded normed algebra, so that displayed claim was outside the licensed setting; it is now restricted to a real Banach space with bounded multiplication.

The rejected definition quantified over every bounded F while applying the local dimension operation to ran F, although that operation is supplied only for finite-dimensional vector spaces. Hence the central quantity a_n(T) was not well-formed. The candidate set now explicitly requires ran F to be finite-dimensional before imposing dim_F ran F<n, and the proof uses exactly that domain.

The supplier states M=(ker T)^perp, H=M direct-sum M^perp, and M^perp as a subset of ker T. Since orthogonality is symmetric, every vector of ker T is orthogonal to M=(ker T)^perp, giving ker T as a subset of M^perp. The asserted decomposition H=(ker T)^perp direct-sum ker T therefore follows from the cited theorem.

reviews.reason: The spectral decomposition, finite-dimensional eigenspaces, and completeness argument were checked against the actual supplier. The equality M^perp=ker T follows by the two inclusions above, so the eigenvectors together with a supplied orthonormal basis of ker T form the claimed Hilbert basis. Its proof, dependencies, contract, and owning page require no edit.

Fact A4 now takes finite 1/n-nets only for integers n>=1, whose union is still countable and dense because every positive radius dominates 1/n for some positive integer n. The reproducing-kernel factorization, basis enumeration, Tonelli calculation, nuclear series, diagonal trace formula, declared dependencies, proof contract, and owning page were checked after that repair.

The multiplication specialization now assumes a real Banach space, so it lies inside the Frechet-derivative interface used by the main bounded-bilinear proof. The bilinear remainder B(h,k) is quadratic in the max norm, and the diagonal specialization is explicitly restricted to X=Y; all supplier uses, the local contract, and the owning page were checked.

The definition and proof now quantify only over bounded operators with finite-dimensional range before applying dim_F. Singular-value truncations supply the upper bound, while rank-nullity on span(e_1,...,e_n) supplies a unit vector killed by each admissible F and hence the lower bound. The infimum hypotheses, field, zero-padded cases, direct consumer, local contract, and owning page were also checked.

The kernel decomposition is a derived consequence of the supplied spectral theorem, not an unsupported strengthening. Positivity makes every nonzero eigenvalue positive, and the singular values of T are therefore precisely those positive eigenvalues with multiplicity; absolute convergence and basis independence then give the trace formula. The dependencies, proof contract, and page interface remain sound.
